parameters.content:
## ListPBX API Reference



Base URL: http://your-serv


er:8080 Version: v1 Content-Type: application/json

Authentication
All /v1/* endpoints require one of two methods.

Method 1 — Bearer JWT (admin web dashboard)
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Issued by POST /auth/login. Expires after 24 hours. Use this for the admin UI only.

Method 2 — API Key (mobile apps, agents, CRM integrations)
X-API-Key: lpbx_<id>_<secret>
Never expires. Create via POST /v1/api-keys in the dashboard. This is the correct method for mobile agents.

Which method should I use?
Who	Method	How to get credentials
Admin web dashboard	Bearer JWT	POST /auth/login → use token
Mobile agent app	API Key	Admin creates key → distribute to agent
CRM / backend server	API Key	Admin creates key → configure in CRM
CI/webhooks	API Key	Admin creates key → store in secrets
Mobile team note: Do not use /auth/login in agent apps. The login endpoint is scoped to the tenant admin and issues a short-lived (24h) token. Instead, the admin creates a long-lived API key per app/agent from the dashboard, and the app sends X-API-Key: lpbx_xxx_yyy on every request. No login flow needed.

Errors
All errors return JSON:

{ "error": "description", "code": 400 }
Code	Meaning
400	Bad request / missing field
401	Missing or invalid credentials
404	Resource not found
409	Conflict (duplicate)
503	No outbound trunk configured
500	Internal error
Auth Endpoints
These endpoints are for the admin web dashboard only. Mobile agents and integrations should use API Keys — see Authentication section above.

Register Tenant
POST /auth/register
Creates a new workspace. Returns a JWT for immediate use.

Request

{
  "name": "Aqary International",
  "domain": "aqary.local",
  "email": "admin@aqary.com",
  "password": "secret"
}
Response 201

{
  "tenant_id": "897464a2-d706-4e8d-a69c-6854e68c7ddb",
  "token": "eyJhbGci..."
}
Login (admin dashboard only)
POST /auth/login
Returns a short-lived JWT (24 h) for the admin dashboard. Not for agent apps — use Agent Login below.

Request

{
  "domain": "aqary.local",
  "password": "your-admin-password"
}
Response 200

{
  "token": "eyJhbGci...",
  "tenant_id": "897464a2-..."
}
Agent Login
POST /auth/agent/login
Authenticates a specific agent (extension) with their extension number or email + SIP password. Returns a JWT that carries the agent's identity — no API key distribution needed.

Use this in mobile apps, softphone apps, or any per-agent client.

Request — by extension number:

{
  "domain": "aqary.local",
  "extension": "1001",
  "password": "AgentPass123"
}
Request — by email:

{
  "domain": "aqary.local",
  "email": "ahmed@aqary.com",
  "password": "AgentPass123"
}
Response 200

{
  "token": "eyJhbGci...",
  "tenant_id": "897464a2-...",
  "extension_id": "3d116d32-...",
  "extension": "1001",
  "name": "Ahmed Al Mansouri"
}
The token embeds the agent's extension. Any subsequent POST /v1/calls made with this token will automatically use "from": "1001" — the agent doesn't need to pass it manually.

Error cases: - 401 — wrong password, extension not found, or account disabled - 401 — extension exists but has no password set (admin hasn't saved credentials yet)

Account
Get Current Tenant
GET /v1/me
Response 200

{
  "id": "897464a2-...",
  "name": "Aqary International",
  "domain": "192.168.1.173"
}
API Keys
API keys are the recommended credential for mobile agent apps, CRM integrations, and backend services. They never expire and do not require a login flow.

How to issue a key for an agent: 1. Admin logs into the dashboard → API Keys → Create 2. Give the key a descriptive name (e.g. "Agent - Ahmed iOS") 3. Copy the key immediately — it is shown once only 4. Paste it into the agent's app config or environment variable

How the agent app uses it — every request:

GET /v1/calls HTTP/1.1
X-API-Key: lpbx_abc12345_<secret>
No token refresh, no login endpoint, no expiry handling needed.

Create API Key
POST /v1/api-keys
Request

{ "name": "Agent - Ahmed iOS" }
Response 201

{
  "id": "abc12345",
  "name": "Agent - Ahmed iOS",
  "key": "lpbx_abc12345_<48-char-hex>",
  "warning": "Store this key securely — it will not be shown again"
}
The raw key is shown once only. Store it immediately.

List API Keys
GET /v1/api-keys
Response 200

{
  "api_keys": [
    {
      "id": "abc12345",
      "name": "CRM Integration",
      "last_used": "2026-04-20T14:00:00Z",
      "created_at": "2026-04-01T10:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
Delete API Key
DELETE /v1/api-keys/:id
Response 204 No Content

Extensions
SIP endpoints (desk phones, softphones, WebRTC clients). Each extension gets a number (e.g. 1001) and SIP credentials.

List Extensions
GET /v1/extensions
Response 200

{
  "extensions": [
    {
      "id": "3d116d32-...",
      "number": "1001",
      "name": "Sales Agent",
      "voicemail": true,
      "call_forward": "",
      "do_not_disturb": false,
      "max_calls": 5,
      "enabled": true,
      "created_at": "2026-04-01T10:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "total": 1
}
Create Extension
POST /v1/extensions
Request

{
  "number": "1001",
  "name": "Sales Agent",
  "password": "Pass1234",
  "max_calls": 5
}
Response 201

{
  "id": "3d116d32-...",
  "number": "1001",
  "name": "Sales Agent"
}
SIP Registration — use these settings in MicroSIP / any SIP client: - Server: your PBX IP (e.g. 192.168.1.173) - Port: 5060 - Username: 1001 - Password: the password set above

Get Extension
GET /v1/extensions/:id
Update Extension
PUT /v1/extensions/:id
All fields optional — only provided fields are updated.

Request

{
  "name": "Senior Agent",
  "call_forward": "+971501234567",
  "do_not_disturb": false,
  "voicemail": true,
  "max_calls": 10,
  "enabled": true
}
Response 200 { "status": "updated" }

Delete Extension
DELETE /v1/extensions/:id
Response 204 No Content

Trunks
SIP trunks connect your PBX to the outside world (PSTN carriers, GSM gateways, Twilio).

List Trunks
GET /v1/trunks
Response 200

{
  "trunks": [
    {
      "id": "...",
      "name": "SIM_CARDS",
      "provider": "generic",
      "host": "192.168.1.69",
      "port": 5060,
      "username": "",
      "from_domain": "192.168.1.173",
      "codecs": ["PCMU", "PCMA"],
      "max_channels": 30,
      "inbound": true,
      "outbound": true,
      "outbound_priority": 1,
      "enabled": true
    }
  ],
  "total": 1
}
Create Trunk
POST /v1/trunks
Request

{
  "name": "SIM_CARDS",
  "provider": "generic",
  "host": "192.168.1.69",
  "port": 5060,
  "username": "",
  "password": "",
  "from_domain": "192.168.1.173",
  "codecs": ["PCMU", "PCMA"],
  "max_channels": 30,
  "inbound": true,
  "outbound": true,
  "outbound_priority": 1
}
Field	Required	Default	Notes
name	✓	—	Unique name, no spaces
host	✓	—	SIP server IP or hostname
provider	—	generic	generic or twilio
port	—	5060	SIP port
outbound_priority	—	10	Lower = preferred (1 beats 10)
Response 201

{ "id": "...", "name": "SIM_CARDS" }
Get / Update / Delete Trunk
GET    /v1/trunks/:id
PUT    /v1/trunks/:id
DELETE /v1/trunks/:id
Trigger FreeSWITCH Rescan
POST /v1/trunks/:id/register
Forces FreeSWITCH to reload gateway config. Call after modifying a trunk.

Response 200 { "status": "rescanning" }

Twilio: List Numbers
POST /v1/trunks/twilio/numbers
Fetches phone numbers from Twilio without exposing credentials to the frontend.

Request

{
  "account_sid": "ACxxxxxxx",
  "auth_token": "your_auth_token"
}
Response 200

{
  "numbers": [
    { "sid": "PNxxx", "friendly_name": "+1 212...", "phone_number": "+12125551234" }
  ]
}
Twilio: Auto-Setup
POST /v1/trunks/twilio/setup
Automatically creates a Twilio Elastic SIP Trunk, sets the origination URL, and assigns phone numbers — all in one call.

Request

{
  "account_sid": "ACxxxxxxx",
  "auth_token": "your_auth_token",
  "server_address": "your.pbx.ip:5060",
  "trunk_name": "ListPBX Main",
  "phone_number_sids": ["PNxxx", "PNyyy"]
}
Response 200

{
  "trunk_sid": "TKxxx",
  "termination_uri": "listpbx-main-a3f2.pstn.twilio.com",
  "sip_url": "sip:your.pbx.ip:5060",
  "assigned": 2,
  "total": 2
}
Inbound Routes
Maps incoming DIDs (phone numbers) to actions. Evaluated in priority order (higher = first).

Route Types
route_type	route_target	Behaviour
extension	Extension number e.g. "1001"	Ring a SIP softphone/phone
ivr	IVR UUID	Play IVR menu
voicemail	Extension number	Go straight to voicemail
masked_bridge	Agent's real number e.g. "+971501234567"	Privacy bridge — both parties see only the DID
hangup	(ignored)	Reject the call
webhook	Webhook URL	POST call details to your endpoint for dynamic routing
Privacy Bridge (masked_bridge)
The core number-masking feature for real estate, recruitment, and any scenario where you need to protect agent/customer numbers:

Lead dials +971503479311  (published DID)
         ↓
  FreeSWITCH receives call
         ↓
  Originates to +971501234567  (agent's real mobile)
  with caller ID = +971503479311
         ↓
  Both legs bridge
         ↓
Lead sees: +971503479311   (dialled it)
Agent sees: +971503479311  (incoming)
Neither sees the other's real number
List Routes
GET /v1/routes
Response 200

{
  "routes": [
    {
      "id": "...",
      "did": "+971503479311",
      "route_type": "masked_bridge",
      "route_target": "+971501234567",
      "trunk_id": null,
      "priority": 10,
      "enabled": true
    }
  ],
  "total": 1
}
Create Route
POST /v1/routes
Request

{
  "did": "+971503479311",
  "route_type": "masked_bridge",
  "route_target": "+971501234567",
  "trunk_id": "<trunk-uuid>",
  "priority": 10
}
Field	Notes
did	Exact E.164 number, or "any" to catch all unmatched calls
route_type	See Route Types table above
route_target	Depends on route_type
trunk_id	Optional. Forces a specific outbound trunk for masked_bridge. Defaults to highest-priority trunk
priority	Higher wins. Use to order fallbacks
Response 201 { "id": "..." }

Get / Update / Delete Route
GET    /v1/routes/:id
PUT    /v1/routes/:id
DELETE /v1/routes/:id
Update Request (all fields optional)

{
  "did": "+971503479311",
  "route_type": "extension",
  "route_target": "1001",
  "priority": 20,
  "enabled": false
}
IVRs
Interactive Voice Response menus with DTMF digit routing.

Create IVR
POST /v1/ivrs
Request

{
  "name": "Main Menu",
  "greeting": "Welcome to Aqary. Press 1 for Sales, 2 for Support.",
  "timeout": 10,
  "max_retries": 3,
  "options": [
    { "digit": "1", "description": "Sales", "route_type": "extension", "route_target": "1001" },
    { "digit": "2", "description": "Support", "route_type": "extension", "route_target": "1002" },
    { "digit": "0", "description": "Operator", "route_type": "extension", "route_target": "1000" }
  ]
}
Response 201 { "id": "...", "name": "Main Menu" }

List / Get / Update / Delete IVR
GET    /v1/ivrs
GET    /v1/ivrs/:id
PUT    /v1/ivrs/:id
DELETE /v1/ivrs/:id
Contacts
Phone book scoped to your tenant. Contact names appear in the call log UI when a number matches.

List Contacts
GET /v1/contacts?search=<query>&limit=200&offset=0
search is optional — matches against name, phone, or company (case-insensitive).

Response 200

{
  "contacts": [
    {
      "id": "c1a2b3c4-...",
      "name": "Jane Smith",
      "phone": "+971501234567",
      "email": "jane@example.com",
      "company": "Acme Corp",
      "notes": "VIP client",
      "created_at": "2026-04-27T10:00:00Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-04-27T10:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "total": 1
}
Create Contact
POST /v1/contacts
Request

{
  "name": "Jane Smith",
  "phone": "+971501234567",
  "email": "jane@example.com",
  "company": "Acme Corp",
  "notes": "VIP client"
}
Field	Required	Notes
name	✓	Display name
phone	✓	E.164 recommended
email	—	Optional
company	—	Optional
notes	—	Optional free-text
Response 201

{ "id": "c1a2b3c4-..." }
Lookup by Phone
GET /v1/contacts/lookup?phone=+971501234567
Finds the first contact whose phone exactly matches. Returns null if not found.

Response 200

{ "contact": { "id": "...", "name": "Jane Smith", ... } }
{ "contact": null }
Get Contact
GET /v1/contacts/:id
Response 200 — full contact object (same shape as list items)

Update Contact
PUT /v1/contacts/:id
All fields optional — only provided fields are updated.

Request

{
  "name": "Jane Doe",
  "phone": "+971509999999",
  "company": "New Corp"
}
Response 200 { "status": "updated" }

Delete Contact
DELETE /v1/contacts/:id
Response 204 No Content

Calls
Dial Outbound Call
POST /v1/calls
Two modes:

Click-to-call (rings agent's SIP phone first, then bridges to PSTN):

{
  "from": "1001",
  "to": "+971501234567",
  "trunk_id": "<optional-trunk-uuid>"
}
Direct dial (PSTN call immediately, no SIP phone involved):

{
  "to": "+971501234567",
  "trunk_id": "<optional-trunk-uuid>"
}
Response 201

{ "call_id": "4ff17660-690c-42f7-bd02-30a289583f04" }
Use call_id to hang up, hold, transfer, or record the call.

List Active Calls
GET /v1/calls
Returns all currently active calls for the tenant.

Response 200

{
  "calls": [
    {
      "id": "4ff17660-...",
      "direction": "outbound",
      "from": "1001",
      "to": "+971501234567",
      "status": "answered",
      "started_at": "2026-04-20T14:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "total": 1
}
Get Call
GET /v1/calls/:id
Checks active calls first, falls back to call history.

Call History
GET /v1/calls/history?limit=50&offset=0
Paginated call logs from the database.

Response 200

{
  "calls": [
    {
      "id": "4ff17660-...",
      "direction": "inbound",
      "from": "+971561751531",
      "to": "+971503479311",
      "status": "hungup",
      "started_at": "2026-04-20T14:00:00Z",
      "answered_at": "2026-04-20T14:00:05Z",
      "hung_up_at": "2026-04-20T14:02:30Z",
      "duration": 145,
      "recording_url": null
    }
  ],
  "limit": 50,
  "offset": 0
}
Hang Up Call
DELETE /v1/calls/:id?cause=NORMAL_CLEARING
Response 200 { "status": "ok" }

Common cause values: NORMAL_CLEARING, USER_BUSY, NO_ANSWER, CALL_REJECTED

Hold / Unhold
POST /v1/calls/:id/hold
POST /v1/calls/:id/unhold
Response 200 { "status": "held" } / { "status": "active" }

Transfer
POST /v1/calls/:id/transfer
Request

{
  "to": "1002",
  "context": "default"
}
Response 200 { "status": "transferred", "to": "1002" }

Start Recording
POST /v1/calls/:id/record
Response 200

{
  "status": "recording",
  "path": "/var/lib/freeswitch/recordings/4ff17660-..._20260420-140000.wav"
}
Stop Recording
DELETE /v1/calls/:id/record
Request (optional — omit to stop all recordings)

{ "path": "/var/lib/freeswitch/recordings/4ff17660-..._20260420-140000.wav" }
Response 200 { "status": "stopped" }

Play Audio / TTS
POST /v1/calls/:id/play
Request — file path:

{ "audio": "/var/lib/freeswitch/sounds/en/us/callie/ivr/ivr-welcome.wav" }
Request — text-to-speech:

{ "tts": "Your call is being transferred. Please hold." }
Response 200 { "status": "playing" }

Bridge Two Calls
POST /v1/calls/:id/bridge
Connects two active call legs (e.g. after consulting a colleague).

Request

{ "call_id": "<second-leg-uuid>" }
Response 200 { "status": "bridged" }

WebSocket — Real-time Events
GET /v1/ws?token=<jwt>
Upgrade to WebSocket. Receives real-time call events for the tenant.

Connection message:

{ "type": "connected", "msg": "ListPBX WebSocket ready" }
Event message format (emitted on every call state change):

{
  "type": "call.ringing",
  "call_uuid": "4ff17660-...",
  "caller_number": "+971561751531",
  "dest_number": "+971503479311",
  "direction": "inbound",
  "timestamp": "2026-04-20T14:00:00Z"
}
Event types:

Type	Trigger
call.ringing	Inbound call arrives or outbound leg starts ringing
call.answered	Call answered
call.hung_up	Call ended
call.recording_ready	Recording file available
call.dtmf	DTMF digit received
call.transcription	Real-time transcription segment
Webhooks
Receive HTTP POST notifications for call events at your own endpoint.

Create Webhook
POST /v1/webhooks
Request

{
  "url": "https://your-crm.com/webhooks/pbx",
  "events": ["call.ringing", "call.answered", "call.hung_up"]
}
Response 201

{
  "id": "...",
  "url": "https://your-crm.com/webhooks/pbx",
  "secret": "a3f2b1c9..."
}
The secret is shown once only. Use it to verify HMAC-SHA256 signatures on incoming webhook POSTs.

Webhook Payload
Your endpoint receives:

POST https://your-crm.com/webhooks/pbx
Content-Type: application/json
X-ListPBX-Signature: sha256=<hmac>

{
  "type": "call.answered",
  "call_uuid": "4ff17660-...",
  "tenant_id": "897464a2-...",
  "caller_number": "+971561751531",
  "dest_number": "+971503479311",
  "direction": "inbound",
  "timestamp": "2026-04-20T14:00:05Z"
}
Verify signature:

import hmac, hashlib
expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
assert f"sha256={expected}" == request.headers["X-ListPBX-Signature"]
List / Update / Delete Webhook
GET    /v1/webhooks
PUT    /v1/webhooks/:id
DELETE /v1/webhooks/:id
Test Webhook
POST /v1/webhooks/:id/test
Sends a synthetic call.ringing event to verify your endpoint is reachable.

Response 200 { "status": "test event sent", "event_type": "call.ringing" }

Utility
Health Check
GET /health
Response 200

{
  "status": "ok",
  "service": "listpbx-api",
  "esl": "connected"
}
esl is "connected" when FreeSWITCH ESL is reachable, "disconnected" otherwise.

Public IP Detection
GET /v1/server/public-ip
Returns the server's public IP — useful for Twilio trunk configuration.

Response 200 { "ip": "1.2.3.4" }

Run FreeSWITCH Command (debug)
GET /internal/fs/cmd?q=sofia+status
Executes any FreeSWITCH API command and returns raw output. Restrict to internal network in production.

Response 200 text/plain

                   Name          Type                                        Data      State
=================================================================================================
               internal       profile          sip:mod_sofia@192.168.1.173:5060      RUNNING (2)
       internal::SIM_CARDS       gateway              sip:FreeSWITCH@192.168.1.69:5060        NOREG
Integration Recipes
CRM Click-to-Call (iframe / web)
// Agent clicks "Call" button in CRM
const res = await fetch('http://pbx:8080/v1/calls', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ from: '1001', to: '+971501234567' })
});
const { call_id } = await res.json();

// Hang up when agent clicks "End"
await fetch(`http://pbx:8080/v1/calls/${call_id}`, {
  method: 'DELETE',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}` }
});
Real-time Call Dashboard (WebSocket)
const ws = new WebSocket(`ws://pbx:8080/v1/ws?token=${token}`);
ws.onmessage = (e) => {
  const event = JSON.parse(e.data);
  if (event.type === 'call.ringing') {
    showIncomingCall(event.caller_number);
  } else if (event.type === 'call.hung_up') {
    removeCallFromDashboard(event.call_uuid);
  }
};
Privacy Bridge — Real Estate Setup
// 1. Create inbound route: when lead calls the published number,
//    bridge them privately to the agent's real mobile
await fetch('/v1/routes', {
  method: 'POST',
  body: JSON.stringify({
    did: '+971503479311',        // published "agent" number
    route_type: 'masked_bridge',
    route_target: '+971501234567', // agent's real mobile
    trunk_id: simCardsTrunkId,
    priority: 10
  })
});

// Both parties see only +971503479311
// Lead's real number is visible to the system (for CRM logging) but not to the agent
// Agent's real mobile is never exposed to the lead
Mobile Agent App Integration
Mobile agents authenticate with an API Key — no login endpoint, no token refresh logic, no expiry.

Setup — agent logs in with their own credentials:

// iOS Swift — agent login on app launch
let body = ["domain": "aqary.local", "extension": "1001", "password": userEnteredPassword]
var loginRequest = URLRequest(url: URL(string: "http://pbx:8080/auth/agent/login")!)
loginRequest.httpMethod = "POST"
loginRequest.setValue("application/json", forHTTPHeaderField: "Content-Type")
loginRequest.httpBody = try! JSONEncoder().encode(body)

URLSession.shared.dataTask(with: loginRequest) { data, _, _ in
    let response = try! JSONDecoder().decode(AgentLoginResponse.self, from: data!)
    // Store token in Keychain — valid 24h, refresh on 401
    Keychain.store("pbx_token", response.token)
    self.agentExtension = response.extension  // "1001"
    self.agentName = response.name
}.resume()
Every API request — use Bearer token:

// iOS Swift — reusable auth header
let token = Keychain.get("pbx_token")
var request = URLRequest(url: URL(string: "http://pbx:8080/v1/calls/history?limit=20")!)
request.setValue("Bearer \(token)", forHTTPHeaderField: "Authorization")

URLSession.shared.dataTask(with: request) { data, _, _ in
    let history = try! JSONDecoder().decode(CallHistoryResponse.self, from: data!)
    DispatchQueue.main.async { self.updateCallLog(history.calls) }
}.resume()
// Android Kotlin — OkHttp interceptor (add once, applies to all calls)
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
    .addInterceptor { chain ->
        val token = tokenStore.get() // your secure storage
        val request = chain.request().newBuilder()
            .addHeader("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
            .build()
        chain.proceed(request)
    }
    .build()
Useful endpoints for agent apps:

What	Endpoint
Recent call history	GET /v1/calls/history?limit=20
Active calls right now	GET /v1/calls
Look up caller name	GET /v1/contacts/lookup?phone=+971501234567
Initiate click-to-call	POST /v1/calls
Hang up a call	DELETE /v1/calls/:id
Real-time events	WS /v1/ws?token=<jwt> (WebSocket requires JWT — request one via login if needed)
Number Format
All phone numbers should be in E.164 format: +<country-code><number>

Example	Meaning
+971501234567	UAE mobile
+971503479311	UAE landline
+12125551234	US number
UAE local format (0501234567) is also accepted and automatically converted internally.

parameters.name: name
parameters.value: ={{ ($('Loop Over Items').item.json.data.First_Name ? $('Loop Over Items').item.json.data.First_Name + ' ' : '') + ($('Loop Over Items').item.json.data.Last_Name || '') }}
